_comment: The test piano's instruments and rooms (piano_render). Installed by `python -m piano_render fetch` (piano_render/fetch.py) under root/<subdir>; files are relative to root. label = what the Room page shows: plain and honest about what was sampled. engine: sfizz (SFZ via libsfizz), fluidsynth (SF2), windows-gs (today's live Windows GS Wavetable synth on PC22; never rendered). onset_ms = the library's own lead-in (first sample above -50 dBFS after a note-on, median over keys and velocities; measured by fetch's builder 22 Oct). velocity_gamma, gain_db, eq, resonance_db: starting values, calibrated by ear later. Rooms: ir = a 48 kHz float WAV under root; 4 channels = true stereo in the order L->L, L->R, R->L, R->R (Samplicity's Bricasti M7 quad files), 2 channels = mono in, stereo out; synth = the synthetic-IR fallback when ir is null or not installed; rt60_s/ir_t30_s = measured T30 (500 Hz-2 kHz, Schroeder) of the IR. Fetch blocks: url, sha256, bytes, unpack (zip|tar|7z|deb|none), subdir; optional strip (leading path parts dropped), members (fnmatch patterns kept), post (a recipe: bitklavier-sfz writes the SFZ map; sfz-wrap writes a wrapper SFZ beside the library's own, per its wrap block: global opcodes, set_cc defaults, replace = exact text fixes, see fetch.post_sfz_wrap). half_pedal: true passes CC64 raw to an SFZ that models half pedalling itself (else on/off at 64). copy_from = a local file copied in (the owner's own SoundFont).

concert-d.label: Concert grand (Steinway D)
concert-d.credit: bitKlavier Grand: a new Steinway D in Princeton University's Taplin Auditorium (2021), recorded by Andrés Villalta, played by Matt Wang, produced by Dan Trueman; Stage Lid ORTF pair (Schoeps), 16 velocity layers every minor third, release resonance, hammer release and pedal samples, 48 kHz/24-bit. CC-BY 4.0. The SFZ map is written by piano_render/fetch.py (bitKlavier ships none).

grand-c5.label: Grand piano (Yamaha C5)

wrap.note: the recommended flat sfz_live set with its sampled release, hammer noise, pedal noise and pedal resonance on at their recorded level (CC20-23 = 127, the author's recommended CC23 for Accurate; off by default); each pedal-noise take gets its own volume, 38 dB under the C4 velocity-64 note through sfizz (measured 22 Oct: down -26.9/-32.7, up -33.4/-39.7)

grand-c5.credit: Accurate-Salamander Grand Piano V6.2a by Chisato Yamauchi: a retuned, level-matched remaster of Alexander Holm's Salamander Grand Piano V3 (Yamaha C5), 16 velocity layers every minor third, hammer and string-resonance release samples, half pedal, pedal noise; sfz_live set, flat voicing, 48 kHz/24-bit FLAC. CC-BY.

bright-cf3.label: Bright concert grand (Yamaha CF3)

wrap.note: sustain pedal on/off at CC64 64, as General MIDI (sfizz's default threshold is 1); note_polyphony=1 moved from <global> to the main notes' <master> (on the release samples too, sfizz 1.2.3 left voices hanging at -94 dBFS after pedalled passages, so renders ran to the 30 s tail cap); the pedal and lid noises (Data/effect.txt, inlined) get a volume per take, 38 dB under the C4 velocity-64 note through sfizz (measured 22 Oct: sustain down -23.3/-22.2, up -38.2/-39.4; sostenuto down -31.1/-33.4, up -42.7/-39.1; the lid noise this SFZ plays on the soft pedal, CC67: open -5.2/-3.1, close -24.5/-14.2)

bright-cf3.credit: Maestro Concert Grand by Mats Helgesson (2003): an early-1990s Yamaha CF-3 sampled on every key, 5 velocity layers, Neumann KM84 X/Y pair, pedal up/down noise; SFZ by sfzinstruments. Free to use, not to sell or redistribute modified (mcgreadme.txt).

steinway-b.label: Steinway B (close, dry)

wrap.note: sustain pedal on/off at CC64 64, as General MIDI (sfizz's default threshold is 1)
sustain pedal on/off at CC64 64, as General MIDI (sfizz's default threshold is 1)

sustain pedal on/off at CC64 64, as General MIDI (sfizz's default threshold is 1); the release samples lose 6 dB per second the key was down (the library's own rt_decay line, commented out, switched on): held back to the pedal lift, 8 of them came in 23 dB above the decayed notes (measured 22 Oct)

steinway-b.credit: VCSL Keys by Versilian Studios (Sam Gossner): an 1895 Steinway Model B, close mics, 3 velocity layers about every second key, separate pedal-down and pedal-up samples, release samples. CC0.

vintage-grand.label: Vintage grand (old Akai samples)
vintage-grand.credit: Splendid Grand Piano: public-domain samples from an old AKAI sample CD (a grand of unstated model, sold as 'Steinway'), 4 layers plus a pedal-down string-resonance group; SFZ by sfzinstruments.

upright.label: Upright piano

wrap.note: sustain pedal on/off at CC64 64, as General MIDI (sfizz's default threshold is 1); the two pedal-noise groups get hikey=-1 (they set lokey=-1 only, so sfizz also played pedal.on.wav on every key); the 30 key-release groups lose polyphony=1 (with it, sfizz 1.2.3 left release voices hanging at about -100 dBFS after pedalled passages, so renders ran to the 30 s tail cap); measured 22 Oct through sfizz against the C4 velocity-64 note: pedal down -32.1 and up -40.8 -> both -38; key-release noise follows velocity fully (amp_veltrack 100, +7.9 dB so velocity 64 stays at -38): after a velocity-20 note it was within 1-4 dB of that soft note in the treble, now 19+ dB under it

upright.credit: K18 Upright Piano by Rudi Fiasco: 6 velocity layers every minor third from A0, key-release noise per sampled key, pedal on/off noise, AB pair, 48 kHz/24-bit. CC-BY 4.0.
